articles.titulo: Life-history trade-offs: the constraints underlying mosquito-borne pathogen transmission.
articles.autores: Johnson B, Jacobs GR, … Murdock C (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mosquito-borne pathogen transmission models typically assume that vector life-history traits vary independently. While survival, reproduction, and immunity are shaped by evolutionary forces to maximize fitness, life-history theory predicts that resource and physiological constraints create trade-offs among these traits. These trade-offs can shape pathogen development and transmission in nonintuitive ways. We argue that incorporating trade-offs into epidemiological and ecological modeling could improve predictive capacity for disease establishment and spread. Environmental variation alters resource allocation and, thus, trait covariation, so environmental variability may have cascading effects on transmission potential. This perspective unifies infection biology, local adaptation, vector-pathogen coevolution, invasion dynamics, and vector control under a common mechanistic framework to improve predictions of disease risk in a rapidly changing world.

v6.implicacao: Alimentação sanguínea de Aedes / Imunometabolismo: dá o enquadramento para tratar competência como resultado de alocação de recursos (dieta/repasto) e não como traço isolado, útil para o Pearl de repasto × doença metabólica; para Epidemiologia de Precisão, é o argumento para modelar covariância entre traços em vez de valores médios.
v6.resumo: Perspectiva que propõe que sobrevivência, reprodução e imunidade do mosquito covariam por restrição de recursos (trade-offs), e que modelos de transmissão que tratam esses traços como independentes perdem previsões não intuitivas; a variação ambiental muda a alocação de recursos e, com ela, o potencial de transmissão.
v6.metodo: Sem dados novos: arcabouço de história de vida para incluir covariância entre traços do vetor em modelos epidemiológicos e ecológicos.

articles.titulo: Maternal and early life obesity programs CD4T cell fate to impair vaccine immunity.
articles.autores: Michieletto MF, Jimenez MT, … Henao-Mejia J (33 autores)
articles.resumo_original: In their first 3 years, children experience an average of 14 infections and receive vaccines against roughly 15 pathogens, yet whether maternal and early life obesity alters adaptive immune responses during this critical period remains largely undefined. Using a mouse model that mirrored the epidemiological link between maternal and childhood obesity, we found that high-fat diet exposure during pregnancy or early postnatal life, but not adulthood, reshaped the epigenetic and transcriptional landscape of naive CD4+ T cells and impaired their ability to differentiate into T follicular helper (TFH) cells and support germinal center reactions in response to mRNA-based and protein-based vaccines. Mechanistically, epigenetic repression of the ubiquitin-editing enzyme A20 (Tnfaip3) was a central driver of these defects. Pediatric patients with haploinsufficiency of A20 displayed a marked reduction in circulating TFH cells. Altogether, these findings establish maternal and early life obesity as determinants of adaptive immunity during a critical developmental window.

v6.implicacao: Imunidade & Memória Imune (priming ontogenético) e Alimentação sanguínea de Aedes / Imunometabolismo: a dieta rica em gordura só reprograma a célula imune dentro de uma janela do desenvolvimento, o que sugere o desenho a testar em Aedes (HFHS na larva ou na mãe versus só no adulto); pergunta concreta de expressão: checar se o ortólogo de A20 (Tnfaip3) muda nos dados de Aag2 e de corpo gorduroso/intestino.
v6.resumo: Em camundongos, dieta hiperlipídica na gestação ou no início da vida pós-natal, mas não na vida adulta, remodela o perfil epigenético e transcricional de células T CD4 virgens e prejudica sua diferenciação em Tfh e a reação de centro germinativo após vacinas de mRNA e de proteína. O mecanismo central é a repressão epigenética de A20 (Tnfaip3); pacientes pediátricos com haploinsuficiência de A20 têm menos células T circulantes.
v6.metodo: Modelo murino com dieta hiperlipídica restrita a janelas de exposição (gestação, pós-natal precoce, adulto), perfil epigenético e transcricional de células T CD4 virgens e imunização com vacinas de mRNA e de proteína; comparação com pacientes com haploinsuficiência de A20.

articles.titulo: Immunometabolic alterations in young adults with obesity are accompanied by divergent monocyte and muscle mitochondrial bioenergetic profiles.
articles.autores: Ursel S, Nekkanti S, … Islam H (14 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Mitochondrial dysfunction and chronic inflammation are implicated in obesity-associated metabolic disorders. Studies interrogating muscle mitochondrial bioenergetics in obesity are confounded by the impact of age and/or physical activity. How obesity impacts mitochondrial bioenergetics in monocytes-precursors to muscle-resident macrophages-is poorly understood. We aimed to compare whole-body immunometabolic function and mitochondrial respiration in muscle and monocytes in adults with or without obesity of similar sex, age and physical activity levels.
In this cross-sectional study, young adults with obesity (BMI ≥ 30) or without obesity (BMI < 30) of similar age, sex and activity levels provided a fasted blood sample and muscle biopsy (vastus lateralis), and underwent a mixed-meal tolerance test. Mitochondrial respiration was measured in permeabilised muscle fibres and blood monocytes using high-resolution respirometry alongside muscle mitochondrial proteins and enzyme activity. Blood monocyte phenotype, polarisation and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS) were quantified using flow cytometry.
Young adults with obesity (n = 17 [9 female/8 male], age 23.1 [SD 5.7] years, BMI 33.2 [SD 3.1] kg/m2) exhibited impaired whole-body insulin sensitivity (d = 1.2) and elevated white blood cell counts (d = 0.9; both p < 0.01) compared with those without obesity (n = 20 [10 female/10 male], age 22.8 [SD 4.6] years, BMI 21.8 [SD 2.1] kg/m2). Muscle oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS; d = 0.7-0.8) and electron transfer system capacity (ETS; d = 1.0) were higher in young adults with obesity than in those without obesity (p < 0.05) despite similar mitochondrial content markers (d = 0.2; p > 0.6). Monocyte OXPHOS (d = 1.0) and ETS (d = 0.8) were attenuated in those with obesity and accompanied by lower Toll-like receptor 4 expression (d = 0.7-0.8), diminished cytokine-stimulated mtROS production (d = 0.8-1.0) (all p < 0.05) and exaggerated proinflammatory marker expression ex vivo (d = 0.8; p = 0.07).
Young adults with obesity exhibit elevated muscle mitochondrial respiration-consistent with early adaptive remodelling in response to energy surplus-accompanied by heightened systemic inflammation and cellular markers suggestive of a dysregulated immunometabolic phenotype.
The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s44357-026-00031-5.

v6.implicacao: Imunometabolismo: precedente em célula imune primária de que excesso de energia reduz a respiração e eleva a resposta pró-inflamatória; respirometria de alta resolução é o método a testar em hemócitos ou Aag2 sob HFHS.
v6.resumo: Adultos jovens com obesidade (n=17) e sem obesidade (n=20), pareados por idade, sexo e atividade, tiveram respiração mitocondrial muscular maior, mas respiração de monócitos menor (OXPHOS e ETS), com menor TLR4, menor mtROS estimulado por citocina e marcadores pró-inflamatórios ex vivo exagerados (p=0,07).
v6.metodo: Respirometria de alta resolução em fibras musculares permeabilizadas e em monócitos do sangue, citometria de fluxo de fenótipo e mtROS, teste de refeição mista.

articles.titulo: Serum context shapes macrophage baseline state and LPS responsiveness in human monocyte-derived macrophages.
articles.autores: Cosma NC, Eren N, … Hellmann-Regen J (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Human monocyte-derived macrophages (MDMs) are central to translational immunology, yet most differentiation protocols rely on xenogeneic fetal calf serum (FCS), which may alter macrophage functional states. Autologous serum (AS) maintains the donor-specific immunometabolic milieu, but its impact on macrophage baseline programming and stimulus responsiveness has not been systematically evaluated.
Monocytes from 32 healthy donors were differentiated in parallel with 10% AS or FCS for five days with M-CSF, followed by 24-hour stimulation with LPS, IL-4/IL-10/TGF-β, or vehicle. Cytokine secretion was quantified by multiplex assay, activation markers by qPCR, and baseline transcriptional programs by bulk RNA sequencing.
AS- versus FCS-differentiated MDMs showed significantly greater LPS-induced secretion of TNF-α, IL-6, IL-1β, IP-10, IL-23, TARC and IL-1RA together with higher CD86 and CCR7 expression, whereas these differences were not observed following IL-4/IL-10/TGF-β stimulation or in unstimulated cells. Transcriptomic analysis of unstimulated MDMs identified distinct serum-dependent baseline programs, with FCS associated with increased expression of inflammatory cytokines, chemokines, and innate immune activation genes, whereas AS was associated with genes involved in lipid metabolism, extracellular matrix remodeling, and immune surveillance.
Serum context is a major determinant of macrophage baseline state and inflammatory responsiveness. FCS is associated with a more inflammatory baseline and attenuated LPS-induced activation, while AS shows a metabolically and immunologically homeostatic baseline with greater LPS responsiveness. These findings demonstrate that serum composition shapes basal macrophage programs and differentially modulates responses to inflammatory versus alternative stimulation, supporting consideration of autologous serum when modeling donor-specific innate immune responses.

v6.resumo: Em macrófagos humanos derivados de monócitos (32 doadores), a diferenciação com soro autólogo em vez de soro fetal bovino muda o estado basal (FCS: mais inflamatório; autólogo: lipídios, matriz, vigilância) e aumenta a resposta a LPS (TNF, IL-6, IL-1β, IP-10, IL-23), sem diferença com IL-4/IL-10/TGF-β.
v6.metodo: Monócitos diferenciados com M-CSF em 10% de soro autólogo ou FCS por 5 dias, estímulo por 24 h, multiplex de citocinas, qPCR e RNA-seq do estado basal.

articles.titulo: Transposons contribute to splice-isoform diversity in thebrain.
articles.autores: Choucri M, Rainey T, Treiber CD (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The extraordinary complexity of the brain depends in part on the vast diversity of mRNA isoforms it expresses, often in a cell-type specific manner. In a recent study, we found that intronic transposable elements (TEs) are spliced into neural transcripts and diversify the splice isoform repertoire of neurons and glia (Treiber and Waddell, 2020). A recent paper by Azad et al. revisits these findings using their TIDAL analysis pipeline applied to our published data (Azad et al., 2024). Their analysis did not find any of the splicing reads we reported and although they used RT-PCR to test seven of the 264 TE-gene pairs we had previously reported, they failed to validate TE-gene splicing in any of them. Here, we conduct a quantitative analysis of TE exonisation and show that intronic TE insertions are frequently recruited as alternative exons, with exon usage ranging from rare events to near-complete inclusion in transcripts. We implement this analysis in an improved version of our TEChim software and present clear support for TE-gene splicing at the seven loci tested by Azad et al. We also identify methodological issues in the experimental and computational design of the Azad et al. study that likely explains their failure to detect TE-gene chimeras, while demonstrating that TE-gene splicing can be detected by RT-PCR under appropriate experimental conditions. Together, our data demonstrates that TE splice isoforms are not rare artefacts but measurable and biologically relevant features of the Drosophila brain transcriptome that may contribute to the molecular complexity and functional adaptability of the brain.

v6.resumo: Réplica de Treiber e Waddell à crítica de Azad et al.: com análise quantitativa de exonização, mostram que inserções intrônicas de elementos transponíveis são recrutadas como éxons alternativos no cérebro de Drosophila, com uso de raro a quase total, e que o RT-PCR valida os sete loci contestados em condições apropriadas. A disputa metodológica segue aberta.
v6.metodo: Reanálise com o TEChim aprimorado e RT-PCR em sete loci TE-gene; ponto metodológico é a sensibilidade de detecção de quimeras TE-gene.

articles.titulo: Molecular screening of arboviruses in asymptomatic blood donors from Northern Brazil.
articles.autores: Calazans AR, da Costa VD, … Alvarez P (20 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Asymptomatic infections caused by the arboviruses dengue virus (DENV), zika virus (ZIKV) and chikungunya virus (CHIKV) pose a hidden risk to blood safety, as viremic donors may contribute to transfusion-transmitted infections with severe outcomes.
Viral RNA from 5,954 pools (each pool contains six samples) was extracted using the Chemagic™ Prime™ platform, as part of the Brazilian NAT PLUS system from pooled plasma samples collected at Amazonas Hematology and Hemotherapy Hospital Foundation (HEMOAM) and analyzed by RT-qPCR using the ZC D-Tipagem molecular assay (Bio-Manguinhos).
Over eighteen consecutive epidemiological weeks, 11 CHIKV-positive cases were identified, 4 DENV-positive cases, and no ZIKV-positive detections on the blood bags samples analyzed.
The detection of asymptomatic arboviral infections during the rainy season, when environmental conditions favor mosquito proliferation and arbovirus transmission, suggests ongoing silent viral circulation in the region and reinforces the importance of blood donor surveillance.

v6.implicacao: Epidemiologia de Precisão (subnotificação): dá uma referência de circulação silenciosa por sangue de doador para comparar com outras fontes de vigilância.
v6.resumo: Em 5.954 pools de seis amostras de doadores do HEMOAM (Amazonas), testados por RT-qPCR ao longo de 18 semanas epidemiológicas, houve 11 pools positivos para CHIKV, 4 para DENV e nenhum para ZIKV, em doadores assintomáticos na estação chuvosa. A positividade é por pool, não por doador.
v6.metodo: RT-qPCR (ZC D-Tipagem, Bio-Manguinhos) em pools de plasma do sistema NAT PLUS.

articles.titulo: Intelligent classification of medically and veterinary important mosquito vectors using self-distillation-enhanced supervised learning.
articles.autores: Chuwongin S, Kaewthamasorn M, … Kittichai V (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mosquito-borne diseases remain a persistent global public health burden, with effective control strategies depending on the accurate and timely identification of mosquito species and estimation of their population density. The current gold standard, morphological identification via microscopic examination, is limited by inter-observer variability and a scarcity of local taxonomic expertise. While highly accurate, molecular techniques like polymerase chain reaction and DNA barcoding are often impractical for widespread field use due to their cost, procedural complexity, and reliance on specialized equipment and technicians. In response to these challenges, this study harnesses the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to develop a robust, accessible diagnostic tool. We introduce an innovative application of the Distillation of knowledge with NO labels v2 (DINOv2-l14) algorithm, a self-supervised learning (SSL) model, for the classification of 30 distinct mosquito species from image data. A key focus was enabling the model to learn effectively from a highly imbalanced dataset, where the number of images per class ranged from 15 to 124. We also investigated the data efficiency of SSL by determining the minimum data partition required to match the performance of a conventional supervised model. Our image processing pipeline involved cropping, padding, and dividing images into 14 × 14 patches before converting them into embedded vectors for classification. The fully trained DINOv2-l14 model significantly outperformed a selected ResNet101 baseline, achieving 99.2% accuracy, 97.7% specificity, an F1 score of 86.1%, and a robust area under the curve (AUC) value of 0.996. Most notably, when fine-tuned on just 20% of the available data (averaging 11-13 images per class), the SSL model achieved performance comparable to the baseline model trained on the entire dataset, demonstrating exceptional data efficiency. Although limitations exist, including dataset imbalance and a lack of standardization for broader application, the model's high performance across five-fold cross-validation and strong Cohen's Kappa coefficients (up to 0.836) confirm its reliability. This work validates a novel, efficient, and highly accurate AI-driven approach to mosquito identification. By integrating such a model into a mobile application using an embedding AI framework, this technology holds significant promise for empowering field personnel with a practical, powerful tool to enhance vector surveillance and control programs worldwide.

v6.implicacao: Ultraestrutura & Bioimagem (análise de dados de imagem): embeddings auto-supervisionados com poucos rótulos são uma via a testar para classificar organelas ou estágios em volumes de EM; o artigo só mostra fotos de mosquito inteiro, então a transferência é hipótese.
v6.resumo: O modelo auto-supervisionado DINOv2-L14 classificou 30 espécies de mosquito a partir de imagens (acurácia 99,2%, F1 86,1%, AUC 0,996) e superou uma ResNet101; com 20% dos dados (11 a 13 imagens por classe) igualou o baseline treinado com tudo. O conjunto é desbalanceado (15 a 124 imagens por classe).
v6.metodo: Recorte e preenchimento das imagens, patches de 14×14 convertidos em embeddings e classificador sobre eles, com validação cruzada em cinco dobras.

articles.titulo: Efficacy of Early Ivermectin Administration in Acute Chikungunya Virus Infection: A Multicenter, Open-Label, Randomized Controlled Trial.
articles.autores: Chusri S, Surasombatpattana S, … Fernandez S (20 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Acute and chronic joint pain is the hallmark of chikungunya virus (CHIKV) infection, often progressing to debilitating persistent joint pain. No approved antiviral therapy is available. We evaluated the clinical and virological efficacy of early ivermectin administration in acute CHIKV infection.
This open-label, randomized trial enrolled and randomized 127 adult patients with acute chikungunya within 72 hours of symptom onset in Thailand. Patients were assigned (1:1) to oral ivermectin (400 µg/kg/day for 3 days) plus standard of care or standard of care alone. Before the 1-month endpoint, 7 patients were lost to follow-up, leaving a finalized complete-case cohort of 120 participants (n = 60 per arm) for primary efficacy analysis. Co-primary outcomes were time to acute joint pain clearance and the proportion of patients with persistent joint pain at 1 month.
Early ivermectin significantly accelerated acute joint pain resolution compared to controls (median 3.5 days [IQR 2, 6] vs 12.0 days [IQR 8, 35]; adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 3.65, 95% CI 2.28, 5.84; p < 0.0001). Ivermectin was associated with a 92% reduction in the odds of persistent joint pain at 1 month (6.6% vs 30%; adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 0.08, 95% CI 0.03, 0.21; p < 0.0001). It also shortened fever clearance (median 2.0 vs 5.0 days; p < 0.0001) and accelerated viral clearance by day 7.
Early ivermectin intervention within 72 hours of symptom onset significantly accelerates clinical recovery, suppresses viral replication, and profoundly reduces persistent joint pain at 1 month. These findings position ivermectin as a promising, scalable therapeutic strategy against CHIKV.
ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06259383 (Retrospectively registered on February 20, 2024 prior to thawing bio-banked samples for sequential assays, laboratory assay and final analysis).
Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06259383..

v6.implicacao: Fator do hospedeiro no repasto: paciente tratado com ivermectina é fonte de sangue com mosquitocida sistêmico, então tratamento prévio é variável de confusão em estudos de competência que usem sangue de pacientes.
v6.resumo: Ensaio aberto randomizado na Tailândia (127 adultos, 120 analisados) com ivermectina 400 µg/kg/dia por 3 dias, iniciada em até 72 h dos sintomas: a dor articular aguda resolveu em mediana de 3,5 contra 12 dias (aHR 3,65), a dor persistente em 1 mês caiu de 30% para 6,6% (aOR 0,08) e a depuração viral até o dia 7 foi mais rápida. Sem cegamento e com registro retrospectivo.
v6.metodo: RCT 1:1 aberto, ivermectina mais cuidado padrão contra cuidado padrão; desfechos co-primários de dor articular e dor persistente; carga viral seriada em amostras biobancadas.

articles.titulo: Profiling cultivable bacteria in Forcipomyia spp. (Diptera: Ceratopogonidae), feeding on the silkworm Antheraea mylitta (Lepidoptera: Saturniidae): insights into possible transmission routes.
articles.autores: Maitra Mazumdar S, Banerjee N, … Mazumdar A (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The co-occurrence of Antheraea mylitta Drury larvae (commonly known as tasar silkworm) and hemolymph-feeding Forcipomyia spp. (commonly known as biting midges) in the same habitat increases the likelihood of interaction and pathogen transmission. This study investigated bacterial species shared between Forcipomyia fuliginosa Meigen, Forcipomyia esakiana Tokunaga, and A. mylitta, with emphasis on potential pathogens affecting silk productivity, a sector valued at USD 220.58 million as of 2022 to 2023. As tasar rearing occurs outdoors, larvae are at risk of a plethora of biotic stressors, from prey and predators to pathogens. Cultivable bacteria were isolated from the gut and salivary glands of adult midges following their feeding on 5th instar silkworm larvae. The bacterial isolates obtained from these 2 tissues were then compared with those recovered from healthy and diseased 5th instar larvae to assess similarities and differences in bacterial composition. Bacterial identification was done using DNA barcoding, colony morphology, and biochemical characterization. The isolates belonged to Firmicutes (Bacillaceae), mainly Bacillus and Lysinibacillus. Common strains included Bacillus cereus FFG1, Bacillus thuringiensis IL4, Lysinibacillus fusiformis FFG3, and Lysinibacillus boronitolerans FFG2, the latter being the most prevalent. Bacillus subtilis FFS5 was found only in the salivary gland of F. fuliginosa, while all gut bacteria were also present in salivary glands. Transmission studies detected B. cereus and B. thuringiensis in adult A. mylitta but not in eggs or early larvae, suggesting unlikely trans-ovarian or trans-stadial transmission and a possible vector-mediated role of Forcipomyia spp. This study provides the first baseline report of their cultivable bacterial communities.

v6.resumo: Bactérias cultiváveis do intestino e das glândulas salivares de Forcipomyia (mosquito-pólvora) que se alimentam de lagartas de Antheraea mylitta: predominam Bacillus e Lysinibacillus, incluindo B. cereus e B. thuringiensis; B. cereus e B. thuringiensis foram detectados em adultos da lagarta após o repasto, mas não em ovos nem em larvas jovens.
v6.metodo: Isolamento em cultura, identificação por DNA barcoding, morfologia de colônia e testes bioquímicos, com ensaio de transmissão em adultos, ovos e larvas.

articles.titulo: A connectome and transcriptome identity shift through a single transcription factor isoform.
articles.autores: Smolin N, Dombrovski M, … von Reyn CR (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The brain exhibits remarkable neuronal diversity. The sheer number of cell types emerging from extensive transcriptional, morphological, and connectome datasets provokes the question of how the brain is capable of generating so many unique identities. Proper neuronal specification and subsequent features of identity, such as wiring, are essential for normal cognitive and behavioral function. However, we still know little about how identity and wiring are encoded within developmental programs. Here, we turn to the visual system of Drosophila melanogaster. We use its unprecedented combination of single-synapse-resolution wiring diagrams from electron microscopy (EM) connectomes and developmental gene expression profiles from single-cell transcriptomic atlases to study the molecular basis of cell-type-specific terminal identity specification and downstream wiring patterns. We integrate analyses of neuronal anatomy, whole-cell electrophysiology, and single-cell RNA sequencing after perturbation (scRNA-Perturb-seq) to establish that the transcription factor broad functions to control terminal features of identity between two visual projection neuron cell types, LPLC1 and LPLC2. We demonstrate the first characterization in functional connectivity changes following changes in neuronal identity specification. We find broad acts through a single isoform (broad-z4) that is selectively expressed in LPLC1 and has the capacity to reprogram the morphology, functional connectivity, and transcriptional identity of postmitotic LPLC2 neurons into an LPLC1-like cell type. Our findings establish a single transcription factor isoform as the smallest unit required to differentiate neuronal identity, a strategy that may be conserved within developmental programs to expand the capacity for cell-type diversity across animal species.

articles.titulo: Anti-ZIKV IgG Subclass Profiles and Anti-DENV IgG Are Associated With Neonatal Outcomes Following ZIKV Infection During Pregnancy.
articles.autores: Antonelli ACB, Peres GBM, … Silveira LAD (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Zika virus (ZIKV) is a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes. Most infected individuals present mild symptoms; however, vertical transmission of ZIKV can lead to Congenital Zika Syndrome (CZS), which includes microcephaly, neurological, hearing, ophthalmological, and morphological abnormalities. Given the high prevalence of dengue virus (DENV) exposure and antibody cross-reactivity among flaviviruses, understanding how maternal humoral antibody profiles relate to neonatal outcomes after ZIKV infection is important. In this exploratory study, we evaluated maternal and neonatal anti-ZIKV total IgG, anti-ZIKV IgG1 and anti-ZIKV IgG3, and anti-DENV IgG reactivity in relation to maternal-neonatal antibody patterns and neonatal outcomes. Samples from pregnant women and their newborns were collected in Brazil, including pregnancies with microcephaly and other clinical or imaging abnormalities. Anti-ZIKV and anti-DENV IgG reactivity was measured by ELISA. Lower neonatal anti-ZIKV IgG3 reactivity was observed in pregnancies with ophthalmological abnormalities in the individual comparison, although this association did not remain significant after false discovery rate adjustment. Lower neonatal anti-DENV IgG reactivity was observed in pregnancies with ophthalmological abnormalities and with any clinical or imaging abnormality, and both associations remained significant after false discovery rate adjustment. These exploratory associations are hypothesis-generating and do not establish functional protection or a causal role for the measured antibody profiles.

articles.titulo: Neural mitochondria size is negatively correlated with sleep duration.
articles.autores: Brecht M (1 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Discharge of fruit fly sleep-promoting neurons is coupled to mitochondrial activity1. In vertebrates, adenosine accumulation resulting from adenosine triphosphate metabolization triggers sleep2. Such observations and theoretical considerations3,4 prompted us to investigate the link between neural mitochondria and sleep duration. To this end, we measured mitochondrial cross-sections in electron microscopy micrographs from publications of nerve or brain mitochondria in 51 mammalian species. There was considerable within-species variability of mitochondrial cross-section areas and we only included species where measurements from at least two publications could be made. Across 50 of the 51 species the average neural mitochondrial cross-section area decreased roughly exponentially with sleep duration (r = -0.76, p < 0.0001). The naked mole rat was an outlier having large brain mitochondria and long sleep. We also observed a significant decrease of sleep duration with body weight, and a multiple linear regression using sleep duration and body weight explained about 64% of the variance of mitochondrial cross-section areas. We suggest that the urge to sleep might be biophysically linked to mitochondrial size and mitochondrial leakage. Specifically, size-related decreases of mitochondrial surface-to-volume-ratio might reduce the need for sleep by decreasing mitochondrial leakage of reactive oxygen species (ROS). We identify neural mitochondrial size as a possible cellular determinant of sleep duration.

articles.titulo: The ATPase YchF regulates the alarmone levels in.
articles.autores: Milanov M, Prucker I, … Koch HG (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Bacteria are constantly challenged by rapid environmental changes and therefore require efficient acclimation strategies for survival. One conserved strategy is the stringent response, which is mainly executed when bacteria face nutrient limitation. Under those conditions, bacteria synthesize the signalling molecules pppGpp and ppGpp, which induce a metabolic adaptation program that regulates multiple cellular processes. While the importance of (p)ppGpp accumulation for stress adaptation is well established, their basal levels are also essential for coordinating metabolism and survival under non-stress conditions. However, how these basal levels are maintained when sufficient nutrients are available is largely unknown. In the current study, we demonstrate that ribosome binding of the (p)ppGpp synthetase RelA is compromised in the absence of the ATPase YchF, which was previously linked to stress response and polyphosphate metabolism. We furthermore show that basal (p)ppGpp levels are reduced in the absence of YchF and that amino acid derivatives, such as serine hydroxamate, inhibit growth of both the ΔychF and ΔrelA strains. However, under minimal-medium conditions or mild amino acid starvation, the ΔychF strain exhibits a more pronounced growth defect than the ΔrelA strain. Biochemical assays reveal that YchF interacts directly with the pseudohydrolase- and TGS-domains of RelA, which potentially promotes RelA binding to the ribosome. In conclusion, our data suggest that YchF serves as a so far unknown regulator of alarmone production in E. coli.

articles.titulo: Molecular surveillance of drug resistance markers inisolates from Ghana.
articles.revista: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
articles.autores: Myers-Hansen JL, Broyles B, … He Q (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The emergence and spread of Plasmodium falciparum drug-resistant parasites remain a significant hurdle to malaria control and elimination. However, how changes in transmission affect the evolution of drug resistance remains incompletely understood. We investigated the spatiotemporal prevalence of drug resistance across three distinct eco-epidemiological zones of Ghana (Guinea Savannah, Forest and Coastal) by characterizing genetic polymorphisms in five drug resistance genes (pfdhfr, pfdhps, pfmdr1, pfk13 and pfmdr2). A total of 764 P. falciparum isolates collected between 2010 and 2017 were analyzed using amplicon sequencing. The artemether lumefantrine (AL) resistance-associated genotypes, pfmdr1-N86 and pfmdr1-N86 F 184D1246, were near fixation in the Forest zone (90-100% and 63.9-100%, respectively). The prevalence of pfmdr1-N86 also increased significantly over time in the Guinea Savannah and Coastal zones (χ2 = 7.13, P<0.05; χ2 = 7.19, P<0.05). Regarding artemisinin (ART) resistance, none of the validated Southeast Asian pfk13 mutations were detected. We also characterized mutations in pfmdr2, another ART resistance-associated gene, for the first time in the Savannah and Forest zones of Ghana. For sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) resistance, the resistance-conferring alleles pfdhps - 540E and pfdhps - 581G occurred at prevalences below 5% and 10%, respectively. Similarly, the pfdhfr/pfdhps-I51R59N108G437E540 haplotype, associated with full SP resistance, was detected in fewer than 5% of parasites. The observed resurgence of parasites carrying the chloroquine (CQ)-sensitive proxy marker pfmdr1-N86, together with the increase in CQ-wildtype marker (pfcrt-K76) prevalence reported in other studies, suggests that CQ sensitivity is re-emerging and may inform future consideration of CQ-based combination therapies. Additionally, the rarity of the pfdhfr/pfdhps-I51R59N108G437E540 and pfdhfr/pfdhps-I51R59N108G437E540G581 haplotypes, driven by the low prevalence of pfdhps - 540E and pfdhps - 581G alleles, supports the continued use of SP for preventive therapy in Ghana.

articles.titulo: Three-dimensional FIB-SEM analysis of the pore network of meso-/macroporous TiO-supported Pt catalysts and its relation to methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation kinetics.
articles.autores: Otani M, Takahashi R, … Matsuda K (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Porous TiO2 supports were synthesized by a sol-gel method using alkyl ketene dimer (AKD) particles as a template (0-5 wt%), and Pt/TiO2 catalysts were prepared by liquid-phase reductive deposition. Focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) tomography showed that, within the templated series, the macropore fraction of the reconstructed 5 µm × 5 µm × 5 µm volumes generally increased from 0.24 (AKD 1 wt%) to 0.77 (AKD 5 wt%), with apparently through-connected macropores in the most porous support, information complementary to N2 sorption. The actual Pt loadings (ICP-MS) were 2.25, 2.09, 1.31, and 1.25 wt% for AKD 0, 1, 3, and 5 wt%, with Pt nanoparticles of about 1-3 nm (TEM). In methylcyclohexane (MCH) dehydrogenation under an H2-rich feed, the reaction was far from equilibrium at 598-623 K, where the per-gram rates decreased in the order AKD 3 > 1 ≥ 0 > 5 wt%; at 623 K the rates per gram of Pt were 1.4-2.1 times higher on the AKD 3 and 5 wt% supports than on the template-free support. Intraparticle diffusion is most likely insignificant for the powder catalysts (Weisz-Prater), and the most macroporous catalyst was less active per Pt than the AKD 3 wt% catalyst at a similar Pt surface density, so the activity differences are associated with the Pt phase rather than with the macropores. A reversible plug-flow analysis gave the same activation energy for all catalysts over 573-623 K (30-32 kJ mol-1). The apparent activation energies (25.7-34.8 kJ mol-1, 523-623 K) were lower than that of a Pt/Al2O3 reference measured with the same apparatus and procedure (58.6 kJ mol-1, 523-598 K); this is a comparison of apparent values, both affected by the approach to equilibrium. As an order-of-magnitude projection that depends on the assumed diffusivity enhancement (3-30-fold), a first-order-equivalent Thiele analysis indicates that such a macropore network would raise the effectiveness factor of millimetre-scale pellets by about 1.6-4.8 times (2.6-3 times for a tenfold enhancement).

articles.titulo: The importance of stomatal complex structure to the early evolution of vessels in angiosperms.
articles.autores: Pautov A, Ivanova A, … Pautova I (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The development and structural variety of stomatal complexes in Trochodendron aralioides, a species with primitive vessels, were studied. Light, scanning and transmission electron microscopy were used. The stomata have large outer ledges which form stomatal cavities. The guard cells that develop through maternal cells division initially lie on a level with the subsidiary cells. Mutual arrangement of stomatal complex cells changes during their growth. The subsidiary cells of mature stomata lie under the stomata and contain large lipid inclusions, which occupy most of their volume. Four generations of stomata were identified. The epidermis is dominated by tertiary and quaternary stomata. They are smaller than the primary and secondary ones and have the narrowest outer ledge apertures. Based upon the notion that the cavities with narrow apertures are able to decrease stomatal conductance and transpiration rate, and large lipid inclusions hinder hydropassive opening of stomata, it was supposed that these structures could be important for the evolution of some plants, i.e., that they could protect their more vulnerable than tracheids primitive vessels from cavitation and thus provide the possibility of their further structure modifications. Besides, stomatal cavities could represent a structural advantage across varying environments. The cavities occur in plants both in humid environments, where they impede the physical blockage of stomatal pores by water, and in arid ones, where they limit water loss. So, stomatal cavities, even when they have appeared in humid environmental conditions, were adaptive for the arid ones, and vice versa. If they have emerged early in plant evolution, they could contribute to the expansion of flowering plants into different environments.

articles.titulo: Correction: Metabolomics of cerebrospinal fluid in pediatric neuroborreliosis: unraveling candidate immunometabolic signatures and diagnostic potential.
articles.revista: Metabolomics : Official journal of the Metabolomic Society
articles.autores: Serrafi A, El Idrissi A, … Szenborn L (13 autores)

articles.titulo: [Echinacoside attenuates microglial pyroptosis after cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in mice by inhibiting STING/NLRP3 pathway].
articles.revista: Zhejiang da xue xue bao. Yi xue ban = Journal of Zhejiang University. Medical sciences
articles.autores: Lu Q, Guo M, … Wang Y (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
To investigate the regulatory effect of echinacoside (ECH) on microglial pyroptosis in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury and its underlying mechanism.
Fifty 8-week-old specific-pathogen-free male C57BL/6 mice were randomly divided into a sham group, a model group, and an ECH intervention group (n=15 per group). A mouse model of transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) was established to mimic cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. The ECH intervention group received ECH (9 mg/kg) for 7 days after modeling. Neurological function, infarct volume, and cerebral blood flow were assessed by Longa neurological deficit scoring, TTC staining, and laser speckle imaging, respectively. The expression levels of proteins related to the NLRP3 inflammasome and the STING signaling pathway were determined by Western blotting and immunohistochemical staining. Microglia were labeled with ionized calcium-binding adaptor molecule-1 (Iba-1), and the proportions of STING-positive and GSDMD-positive microglia were determined by double immunofluorescence colocalization staining. GSDMD-mediated membrane pore formation was observed by transmission electron microscopy.
Compared with the model group, the ECH intervention group showed improved neurological deficit scores, reduced infarct volume, and restored cerebral blood flow (all P<0.01). ECH significantly downregulated the expression of NLRP3, apoptosis-associated speck-like protein containing a CARD domain (ASC), cleaved caspase-1, GSDMD, STING, phosphorylated nuclear factor-κB p65, and monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (all P<0.01). Double immunofluorescence colocalization showed that GSDMD and STING were co-expressed with Iba-1, respectively, indicating that pyroptosis and STING pathway activation occurred predominantly in microglia. Transmission electron microscopy revealed that ECH reduced GSDMD-mediated membrane pore formation in microglia.
ECH may inhibit microglial pyroptosis by suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation and the STING signaling pathway.

articles.titulo: Metabolic Reprogramming in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Liver-Specific Immune Dysfunction, Immunotherapy Resistance, and Translational Biomarker Development.
articles.autores: Dai C, Lou S, … Xu X (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) arises in chronically injured, often fibrotic or cirrhotic liver, where metabolism, immunity, vascular and stromal organization, disease etiology, tumor state, and hepatic reserve are tightly interconnected. Although immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based therapies have expanded treatment options for advanced HCC, responses remain heterogeneous because of both primary and acquired resistance. Metabolic reprogramming may shape these outcomes by altering nutrient availability, metabolite accumulation, antigen presentation, immune-cell fitness, stromal organization, and spatial immune access. This review provides an evidence-weighted assessment of major immunometabolic mechanisms in HCC, focusing on the glycolysis-hypoxia-lactate and tryptophan-kynurenine/IDO1 axes, lipid and cholesterol metabolism, purinergic signaling, mitochondrial and redox regulation, and ferroptosis. We emphasize that these pathways are context dependent, with effects determined by cellular source, differentiation state, spatial organization, and tumor-intrinsic versus immune-cell metabolic adaptation. Molecular heterogeneity, etiology, and cirrhosis are considered together, with WNT-β-catenin/CTNNB1-associated states illustrating their intersection with immune organization and ICI response. Because translational maturity varies widely, we distinguish mechanistic evidence, biomarker association, predictive validation, and clinical utility. We propose a framework integrating HCC specificity, primary human validation, cellular and spatial localization, causal immune-functional evidence, treatment-linked and longitudinal assessment, biomarker feasibility, and liver-specific safety. The framework also considers intervention timing and the distinction between primary and acquired ICI resistance. It may guide progression from metabolic discovery to spatially resolved mechanism, biomarker development, pharmacodynamic validation, and clinical evaluation while accounting for cirrhosis-associated remodeling, hepatic reserve, and treatment-related toxicity.

articles.titulo: Killer lifestyle: natural killer cells, obesity, and HIV/simian immunodeficiency virus infections.
articles.revista: Current opinion in HIV and AIDS
articles.autores: Beaumont E, Daira M, … Apetrei C (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
The success of antiretroviral therapy (ART) that transformed HIV infection in a chronic clinical condition, and reversed the typical failure to thrive characteristic for HIV disease progression to weight gains, resulted in new challenges for the clinical management of the persons living with HIV (PLWH). Prolonged survival also dramatically increased the average age of PLWH, and the frequency of comorbidities associated with HIV. Most of these clinical challenges stem from the persistent inflammation and accelerated aging characteristic to PLWH, which are also associated with obesity.
Natural killer (NK) cells, which suffer multiple alterations during HIV infection and in obese people, such as a reduction in the frequency of circulating NK cells, alterations in their surface receptor repertoire and expression, unbalanced anti and proinflammatory profiles, with a dysregulated cytokine production. In the meantime, while NK cells are increasingly activated, their functionality (i.e., cytotoxicity) is impaired and their metabolism is altered in obese individuals and in PLWH.
These multiple effects of HIV and obesity on NK cells call for interventions aimed at reversing the immunometabolic reprograming. Multiple such interventions are currently tested, and their impact on the NK cells functionality is still to be evaluated.

articles.titulo: Matrix-matching calibration determination of cadmium using coral reef-like FeOOH-based preconcentration in Antarctic lake water samples.
articles.autores: Kılıçlı CK, Bağlı Ş, … Bakırdere S (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: In this work, solid-phase extraction based on iron oxyhydroxide (FeOOH) nanoparticles were used to extract and pre-concentrate cadmium ions in a precise and sensitive manner. The sensitivity and accuracy of the developed method have increased compared to conventional flame atomic absorption spectrophotometry (FAAS). The improved method provides simple, economic and efficient procedure for the determination of cadmium ions. FeOOH nanoparticles were synthesized by using a hydrothermal route. The nano-sized structure of the FeOOH was as indicated by X-ray diffraction analysis and scanning electron microscopy. Numerous variables, including the medium's pH, the amount of sorbent, mixing type and time, the eluent concentration/volume were optimized using a univariate approach. Optimal conditions resulted in limits of detection and quantification of 0.24 and 0.79 μg/L, respectively. Real samples were obtained from two different lakes (Horseshoe Island, Antarctica) and recovery experiments were performed for the accuracy check. Recovery percentages were calculated using the matrix matching method and high percent recovery results between 85.3 and 113.5% demonstrated the applicability and accuracy of the developed method for cadmium determination in complex environmental matrices.

articles.titulo: Toward Sustainable Production of Reduced Phosphorus Compounds.
articles.autores: Löwe P, Cummins CC (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Although phosphate is the thermodynamically stable and overwhelmingly abundant form of phosphorus in Nature, the modern phosphorus chemicals industry still relies heavily on white phosphorus (P4) as its central feedstock. In the thermal process, phosphate rock is reduced with coke and silica at temperatures around 1500 °C to produce P4, which is then converted to intermediates such as PCl3 before further conversion to value-added phosphorus compounds. This reaction sequence is effective, but involves the reduction of phosphate under high temperature, followed by additional redox and functionalization steps before many target phosphorus compounds are obtained. We therefore asked whether phosphate-derived feedstocks could be converted more directly into reduced phosphorus compounds, making the production of P4 as an intermediate unnecessary while retaining the synthetic flexibility needed for producing a large variety of phosphorus compounds. That question led to three areas of investigation. The first exploits the strong thermodynamic driving force of Si-O bond formation to achieve oxygen-abstraction reduction of phosphate-derived substrates. This led to the discovery of the bis(trichlorosilyl)phosphide anion,[P(SiCl3)2]-, a previously unknown P(-3) synthon that can now be accessed from trimetaphosphate, orthophosphate salts, and phosphoric acid. It can be further converted to value-added phosphorus compounds, such as phosphines, hexafluorophosphate, or phosphonium salts. Protonation of [P(SiCl3)2]- gives bis(trichlorosilyl)phosphine,HP(SiCl3)2, which undergoes selective radical hydrophosphination and gives synthetic access to primary phosphines, chlorophosphines, phosphinic acids, phosphonic acids, and phosphonium salts. The second strategy uses mechanochemistry to convert condensed phosphates directly to phosphite through hydride phosphorylation. Ball milling with alkali-metal hydrides provides a solvent-free route to a P(III) product while retaining the PO3 framework of the starting material. This route also works with biologically recovered polyphosphate feedstocks, which is important for the recycling of sewage sludge. The same mechanochemical platform further proved useful for the analogous redox-neutral phosphorylation of acetylides, giving alkynyl phosphonates directly from condensed phosphates. Finally, strongly reducing mechanochemical conditions based on supported alkali-metal dispersions gave access to ortho-phosphite,PO33-, a previously "missing" phosphorus oxoanion. This new anion can be converted further to phosphite salts, tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite, and alkyl phosphonates. Taken together, these studies show that condensed phosphates and phosphoric acid can be directly used as feedstocks for synthetic phosphorus chemistry, without relying on P4 as an intermediate. This approach enables the identification of reactions that preserve P-O bonds where desirable and creates new opportunities to link phosphorus recovery from waste streams with the synthesis of value-added phosphorus compounds. Determining whether such routes are also more sustainable relative to established manufacturing processes will require a comparative assessment of energy demand, reagent production, waste generation, and process hazards.

articles.titulo: Survival following 14% Plasmodium falciparum hyperparasitaemia: cerebral malaria and anaemic heart failure in a Nigerian toddler.
articles.autores: Unuane AE, Adedosu NA, … Adewuyi GM (12 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Malaria remains a leading cause of mortality amongst children under five in sub-Saharan Africa. Complicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria frequently presents with multiple life-threatening sequelae, including cerebral malaria, profound anaemia, and hyperparasitaemia. Although parasite densities exceeding 10% are independently associated with high mortality, achieving full recovery in a young child presenting with simultaneous extreme parasitaemia, deep coma, and severe malarial anaemia remains exceptionally noteworthy.
We report the case of a 20-month-old male from Akoko, Ondo State, Nigeria, who presented with a five-day history of fever, cough, and diarrhoea, progressing to unconsciousness. Clinical examination revealed a Blantyre Coma Scale of 2/5, profound pallor, tachycardia (158 bpm), and tender hepatomegaly. Laboratory investigations confirmed an extreme 14% P. falciparum parasitaemia and a life-threatening packed cell volume of 8%. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis ruled out bacterial meningitis though an elevated protein level (71 mg/dL) supported the diagnosis of cerebral malaria.
The patient was stabilised in the cardiac position to optimise venous return and alleviate signs of incipient heart failure, and was initiated on a multi-modal therapeutic regimen. Antimalarial therapy was commenced with intravenous artesunate (3 mg/kg), supported by two sessions of sedimented red blood cell transfusions and empiric IV Ceftriaxone. By the fourth day of treatment, the child regained full consciousness and was transitioned to oral artemether-lumefantrine. The patient was discharged in a stable condition on day seven with a recovered packed cell volume of 35%.
This case highlights the critical importance of the "24-h window" in treating severe malaria. The successful outcome confirms the efficacy of intravenous artesunate and the necessity of aggressive supportive care-including blood transfusion-in managing the severe triad of hyperparasitaemia, cerebral sequestration, and severe anaemia in paediatric patients within endemic regions. This report emphasises the need for public health initiatives that educate caregivers on the early recognition of malaria symptoms to facilitate prompt care. Furthermore, it reaffirms that urgent microscopic evaluation remains the gold standard for the immediate diagnosis of hyperparasitaemic cases in resource-limited settings.

articles.titulo: Novel EGCG Analog Modulates Host Immune Response to Promote Intracellular Clearance of Staphylococcus Aureus Through Interaction With the 67-kDa Laminin Receptor.
articles.autores: Grosso R, Ahmed SK, … Wong-Beringer A (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia (SAB) is a leading cause of sepsis. Intracellular bacterial survival in liver macrophages contributes to persistent bacteremia. We evaluated the immunometabolic action of EGCG epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), a green tea polyphenol, and its synthetic analogs (MCC-2 and MCC-4) and the putative target, 67-kDa laminin receptor (67LR).
Murine Kupffer cells (KCs) were infected with live or heat-killed MRSA and treated with study compounds alone or in combination with vancomycin. Intracellular bacterial clearance was assessed at 0, 10, and 24 h post-treatment. KCs were challenged with heat-killed SA when evaluating compound immunometabolic activity: ROS generation using dihydroethidium fluorescence, TNF-α and IL-10 production by ELISA, and mitochondrial biogenesis markers (PGC-1 α, TFAM, mtDNA) by qRT-PCR, and MitoTracker assays. The role of 67LR mediating immunometabolic action was investigated by receptor disruption and binding studies via computational docking and surface plasmon resonance (SPR).
MCC-2 enhanced KC-mediated intracellular MRSA clearance by 1.07 log CFU reduction when combined with vancomycin compared to vancomycin alone. Enhanced clearance was accompanied by up to a 269% increase in ROS generation, a 3.4-fold increase in the TNF-α/IL-10 ratio, and a 25% increase in mitochondrial mass. Receptor disruption and binding studies suggest that MCC-2 activity is mediated partially via 67LR. MCC-4 showed similar mitochondrial activating effects as MCC-2 but was devoid of any antibacterial or immune enhancing activity.
MCC-2 demonstrates promise for further development as an adjunct candidate to antibiotic therapy given its immunometabolic action in enhancing macrophage antimicrobial function while restoring mitochondrial competence through the putative target, 67LR.

articles.titulo: Mature dendrites can function without their mitochondria under ideal conditions.
articles.autores: Harbauer AB (1 autores)
articles.resumo_original: In this issue, Wang et al. (https://doi.org/10.1083/jcb.202511010) show that adult Drosophila horizontal system dendrites remain structurally and functionally intact despite mitochondrial depletion, contrasting with the necessity of mitochondria during development. Their findings suggest that visual system functionality does not require mitochondrial functions under ideal conditions.

articles.titulo: The Muheza Approach: A 7-Year Experience of Sustainable and Affordable Mesh Hernia Surgery in a Lower-Middle Income Country.
articles.autores: Pickering O, Michael B, … Szymankiewicz M (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Hernias are a public health priority in Africa, with a focus on hernia surgery providing the potential to reduce the significant burden of hernia-related morbidity. Only a minority of patients in Africa are currently receiving a gold-standard mesh repair, owing to the cost of commercial mesh. In this study, we describe the long-term outcomes for patients undergoing hernia repairs utilising an affordable polyethylene 'mosquito-net' mesh (MNM) in Muheza, Tanzania.
Data from consecutive patients undergoing MNM hernia repair in a single centre in Muheza between November 2018 and February 2026 were recorded in a prospectively maintained database. Operative technique using a tension-free sublay technique and postoperative care, where feasible, was standardised. Follow-up was performed through a mix of face-to-face and telephone consultation.
A total of 268 hernia repairs were included in the final analysis with a 596-day median follow-up. Most cases were inguinal hernias (89.9%) and primary repairs (85.1%). Thirty-day morbidity rate was 3.5%, including one (0.4%) mesh infection and two patients (0.7%) who required a return to theatre. Chronic pain was reported in 17 (6.3%) patients. There was one hernia recurrence during the study period.
Following our reporting of the early results in 2020, we now offer the longer-term data to demonstrate that the Muheza Approach to hernias utilising MNM is a safe, effective, affordable and sustainable strategy that could provide a platform for wider implementation across LMICs to address the shortfall in high-quality hernia surgery.

articles.titulo: Kinetically controlled boron carbide composite sub-micrometer particle formation pathways during continuous-flow laser melting in liquids with high-power lasers.
articles.autores: Koch NG, Rehbock C, … Barcikowski S (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Monodisperse, spherical sub-micrometer particles with clean, smooth surfaces are key materials used as composite reinforcements, abrasives, and tribological additives, but remain synthetically challenging to produce. Pulsed laser melting in liquids (LML) is an environmentally friendly, emerging route for producing such particles. However, demonstrations have so far been limited to batch reactors, which are difficult to scale up to industrial production. Here, we extend laser melting in liquids to a continuous flat jet flow-through reactor in which boron carbide composite nanoparticles (B4CC) dispersed in ethanol are fed perpendicular to a nanosecond pulsed high-power ultraviolet laser beam; this is complemented by additional experiments employing pristine boron carbide. We elucidate how flow conditions and the application of modern high-repetition-rate lasers alter particle formation pathways. Characterization of B4CC, irradiated at fluences of 45-135 mJ·cm-2, by transmission electron microscopy and dynamic light scattering, evidences the formation of a bimodal size distribution of spherical particles with mean diameters of ≈50 and ≈100 nm, verifying the parallel occurrence of isochoric reshaping and an aggregation-melting-fusion mechanism. While the smaller particle size fraction formed in accordance with thermal equilibrium calculations, the second size mode, derived from a multistep aggregation-melt-fusion pathway, was significantly smaller than predicted. Systematic variation of the number of laser pulses per unit volume (PPV) from 1 to 16 by tuning the interpulse delay (τIP) from 1.4 to 0.1 ms revealed an initial increase of the mean diameter of the second mode with PPV, reaching maximum size at 4 PPV. Interestingly, at higher PPV, further particle growth is arrested, probably due to an interplay between low particle mass concentration and shorter τIP limiting the number of aggregation-melt-fusion steps, indicating kinetically controlled particle formation pathways. If the laser fluence is increased to 180 mJ·cm-2, laser fragmentation in liquid prevails, and small mass fractions of ultrasmall nanoparticles (approx. 2 nm) are formed, which constitutes the upper limit of the LML process window. Overall, at the example of the ultrahard material boron carbide, difficult to process by other methods into perfect spheres, kinetically controlled LML in a flat jet flow-through reactor gives access to nanostructures in a size range previously unattainable by laser processing, establishing the basis for upscaling production in liquid flow with matched laser pulse numbers.

articles.titulo: Longitudinal Dynamics of Circulating NET-Associated Biomarkers and Their Association with Progressive Perihematomal Edema After Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
articles.autores: Wei N, Yang J, … Zhang X (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
In patients with spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (sICH), perihematomal edema (PHE) is a major driver of secondary brain injury, yet the temporal dynamics of circulating neutrophil extracellular trap (NET)-associated biomarkers and their clinical relevance to PHE progression remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize their longitudinal dynamics and associations with PHE progression and clinical outcomes after sICH.
In this prospective cohort study, 200 patients with sICH (70 surgical and 130 non-surgical) and 50 healthy controls were enrolled, with serial peripheral blood samples collected at four predefined time points. Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA), citrullinated histone H3 (CitH3), myeloperoxidase-DNA (MPO-DNA), and neutrophil elastase-DNA (NE-DNA) complexes were quantified. NET-associated neutrophil phenotypes were characterized by flow cytometry, with scanning electron microscopy for complementary ultrastructural assessment. PHE volume was quantified using 3D Slicer, and 90-day functional outcomes were assessed. In the non-surgical cohort, five regression algorithms were compared for exploratory estimation of peak PHE volume from baseline features using all 36 baseline variables within nested cross-validation. SHAP was used to interpret the best-performing model.
Circulating NET-associated biomarkers were markedly elevated in patients with sICH (all P < 0.001), with descriptive plots suggesting different temporal patterns in the surgical and non-surgical subgroups. SEM revealed NET-like extracellular ultrastructures in peripheral neutrophils. In the non-surgical cohort, PHEV was highest at T3 (3-5 days after onset) among the four scheduled assessments; baseline MPO-DNA was strongly correlated with peak PHE volume (ρ = 0.76, P < 0.001) and remained independently associated after multivariable adjustment. Within the non-surgical cohort, exploratory machine-learning analysis identified CitH3, MPO-DNA, and hematoma volume as the top-ranked contributors to peak PHEV estimation. Higher baseline MPO-DNA was also independently associated with unfavorable 90-day functional outcome in this cohort.
Circulating NET-associated biomarkers showed temporal changes after sICH. In the non-surgical cohort, higher baseline MPO-DNA was associated with greater peak PHEV and unfavorable 90-day functional outcome. These findings point to a biological link that larger multicenter studies now need to confirm; the machine-learning findings remain exploratory and require external validation before clinical application.

articles.titulo: Cohort profile: Assessment of factors impacting on foetal and infant immunity, growth, and neurodevelopment in HIV and antiretroviral drug exposed uninfected children: The Siyakhula Study.
articles.autores: du Toit L, Molokoane F, … Rossouw T (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original: This cohort profile paper describes the Siyakhula cohort, a prospective longitudinal study of mother-child dyads during the ante- and postpartum period. The cohort was established to investigate how in-utero and early postnatal environments altered by maternal HIV status influence infants' growth trajectories, cognitive development, immune development and function, irrespective of the infant's HIV status. Pregnant women aged ≥18 years with singleton pregnancies at <22 weeks' gestation (as per best obstetric estimate, including ultrasound), regardless of HIV status, were recruited from January 2018 to January 2021 and followed throughout pregnancy. After delivery, women were approached for continued enrolment in the postpartum arm, which followed the dyads for 24 months. A total of 315 pregnant women (152 living with HIV and 163 without HIV) were recruited. Routine (pregnancy-related clinical data, HIV status, anthropometry) and research-specific (socio-demographic information, body composition analysis, diet, vaginal swabs, bloods) were collected antepartum. Cord blood and placental samples were collected intrapartum, while breast milk, stool samples, and blood were collected postpartum. Infants had anthropometric measurements performed at 6, 10 and 14 weeks, as well as 6, 12 and 24 months. Neurodevelopmental assessments were conducted during later follow-up visits. Extensive clinical, immunological, metabolomic, nutritional, and developmental data, together with a large biorepository of maternal and infant biospecimens, have been established. This paper provides an overview of the cohort design, participant characteristics, available data and biospecimens, completed analyses, and future research opportunities. Future plans include developing immunometabolic signatures associated with optimal and suboptimal growth and neurodevelopment of infants in the first two years of life.
